shorts_extract.hook: Why walking ten feet into the kitchen erases what you came for—while walking ten feet inside one room leaves memory intact.
shorts_extract.core_experiment: Radvansky, Krawietz & Tamplin (2011, Notre Dame): 60 volunteers carrying hidden shoebox objects hit 28% errors through doorways vs 23% across one room.
shorts_extract.twist: Zheng et al. (2022) caught human hippocampal boundary cells filing the old room away on the threshold—a sign of healthy brain organization, not memory loss.
